defects.problem: EXT: Wikipedia’s sonatina paragraph says the usual thematic contrast is absent because of the material’s character; Larner identifies work on the opening bass in the middle, and the Biamonti analysis explicitly describes two related themes and a development. INFERENCE: Turning sonatina into categorical claims of no development and no new tune overstates the source and erases the central passage’s developmental work.
defects.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_Sonata_No._30_(Beethoven) — Prestissimo paragraph. https://geraldlarner.com/work/beethoven-sonata-in-e-major-op-109 — middle section draws material from the first theme’s bass. https://www.lvbeethoven.org/Opus109/ — Biamonti description: related themes, development and recapitulation. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/51/IMSLP51804-PMLP01487-Beethoven_Werke_Breitkopf_Serie_16_No_153_Op_109.pdf — printed pp. 101–103, contrasting register/voice-leading and the central contrapuntal passage.
defects.fix: Replace the categorical no-development/no-new-tune narrative with a compact sonata account: closely related E-minor and B-minor subject material, a central passage developing the opening bass and preparing the return, and recapitulation in E minor. If retaining sonatina as an alternative reading, attribute and qualify it instead of treating it as proof that no developmental work occurs. Update the intro, question and every dependent cue/transition together.
